text:
adir_release: heads-up: deploybot detected error-rate bump on a canary route during the change window. Autorevert threshold is close. Can we decide manual vs auto?

deploybot: ALERT: Canary error-rate (/classify) increased to 1.6% (threshold 1.0%). Autorevert in 60s. See: https://telemetry/deploys/1731119

nina_sre: oncall. Are these 5xxs or client errors?

omar_engineer: 5xx from model runtime on a small subset of carriers. Likely regression from routing logic introduced in PR 512. No widespread latency impact yet.

rachel_pm: Reminder: change window still open for 10m; customers on premium routes might be affected if it hits prod. If we hold, we need a comm plan.

adir_release: propose: apply short hold (5m) to attempt a fast revert of PR 512 on canary, run smoke, then either promote or let autorevert run. If we touch prod, we'll pin route first.

nina_sre: I'll apply hold. `deploybot override --thread 1731119999 --hold 300 --reason "revert PR512 investigation"`

deploybot: ACTION: Autorevert HOLD applied by nina_sre for 300s.

omar_engineer: reverting now: `git revert -m 1 512 && infra/deploy --env canary --tag v4.0.1-rollback`

adir_release: please add a release-note fragment: "Hotfix: reverted routing change that caused intermittent 5xx on /classify; no customer impact expected." I'll also draft CSM ping in #customer-ops.

omar_engineer: revert deployed at 1731120042, smoke ok: 0.2% errors.

rachel_pm: good. estimate 5m to monitor then cancel hold.

nina_sre: `deploybot override --thread 1731119999 --hold-cancel`

deploybot: NOTICE: Autorevert HOLD canceled by nina_sre. Normal policy restored.

adir_release: promoted update to canary and posted PR link in #release-notes. Closing thread; will open follow-up to add a preflight check for routing changes."
